best_for: Signal users who already have the app on their phone and want to type and call from a Windows PC or Mac.

points.title: Your phone comes first
points.text: Signal Desktop is a linked device. You must install Signal on Android or iOS first and then link the desktop app to that account.

points.title: End-to-end encrypted
points.text: Messages and calls use the open source Signal Protocol, so Signal says it cannot read or hear them.

points.title: Free, no ads
points.text: Signal is a nonprofit funded by grants and donations. There are no ads, affiliate marketers or tracking, and the desktop code is AGPLv3.

points.title: Windows installs per user
points.text: The Windows build is a 64-bit installer for the current user only, with no machine-wide option. That suits PCs where you lack admin rights but not shared lab machines.

points.title: Mac and Linux
points.text: Macs need macOS 13, with Intel and Apple silicon builds. Signal also ships Linux builds through its own apt repository and an AppImage, which this site does not list.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 285 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
